questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to combine a university with high academic standards with an interesting city. Montreal has been mentioned as one of the best student cities because of the vibrant and very livable city with lots of you people and good universities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My exchange semester has been postponed because of covid and all the administrative procedures before going were definitely very time consuming and frustrating. But as soon as you finally get there, it is really worth all the work.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Check ArriveCan and you should be good to go!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: McGill has a service mail and they usually answer pretty quick if you need help. I was also offered a 'buddy' (a fulltime McGill student) who could help me if I had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think covid has made everthing complicated, which also affected the orientation assistance at my host institution. You had to be proactive and reach out yourself if you needed information, but that wasn't really a problem.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. There are lots of Facebook groups and the prices are not too high (but be aware of scam - for example by arrange a FaceTime call before signing any contracts).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I really recommend living off campus. It's way less expensive and there are so many cool areas off campus. Personally I was also happy to skip mandatory meal plans and lots of rules in the student residencies.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can really recommend living in Plateau or Mile End.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: McGill's registration system is not the most intuitive system I have ever seen, so you have to be a bit patient.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: McGill's registration system is not the most intuitive system I have ever seen, so you have to be a bit patient. Also, you should consider starting the process long time ahead of the deadline, since you need to gather a lot of documents from your home university etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could often click on small question marks if you didn't understand something and then a help tap would appear. Also, you could always contact the administration from McGill. They are very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. The classed I wanted were only available in the fall (where I was supposed to go if it wasn't for covid). However, I got some other very cool classes instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't hesitate to contact the professors directly if you have problems registering to a class (because of prerequisites). I experienced that they would often let me join their classes if I explained my motivation and qualifications by email.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very interesting!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There were a lot of deadlines and much more participation grates than we're used to from University of Copenhagen. The level was higher than expected (from what you often hear about going abroad). That being said, I still didn't have the feeling that it was too difficult (maybe because we only had to pass the courses)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I really like the engagement of the professors. Also, office hours seems to be a big thing compared to UCPH. The professors were always willing to arrange a one on one talk, which was super helpful if there was something I wanted to understand/discuss more.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: People analytics, Oral and written French 2, Topics in International Business, Social Inquiry

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: People analytics was a really interesting course. The professor Matisse Hollister is really engaged and we touched upon so many interesting feels concerning Artificial Intelligence and ethics in Social data science.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ended up going quite a few one day ski trips, which was really nice but also a bit expensive. Also, grocery stores are a bit more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out. Coffee at cafes (more like 25 DKK compared to 40 DKK in DK)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There seems to be many opportunities if you reach out yourself but because of Covid the opportunities were limited.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Running clubs, French conversation cafes, friday bars etc...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
During winter: go on hikes and ski trips
Summer: chill in the parcs, bike around (the BIXI systems works very well), enjoy the wide range of festivals and concerts

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: rent a chalet outside montreal for a weekend with a group of friends, take the night bus to NYC, visit Vancouver

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Montreal is very international, so a lot of people have the same mindset as yourself. I met a lot of good friends outside university

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
People are really friendly and open, so just talk to people in your classes or at cafes/bars.
Otherwise, there are lots of running clubs (e.g the 6am running club).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much really. I think Montreal in general is a very easy city to adapt to. If anything, it would be helpful to at least try to speak french (for me this was a bit challenging here because of all the Quebecois slang, but people just appreciate that you try)!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
People are used to the fact that people come from all over the world, so it's not a big deal where you're from, which I really appreciated. In general I experienced that people were very open minded and you could easily end up having a good conversation with a stranger in the super market which is definitely different from DK.

Furthermore, I like the french/european touch on Montreal, which you can sense in the language as well as the mindset and culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) enjoy the classes and the professors genuine interest to help you
2) spend more time in plateau and mile end than downtown
3) try to practice your french. That makes the experience much more fun

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring all your woolen clothes for the winters :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the great people I've met from all over the world and the opportunity to get to know a new city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping up with all the deadlines.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
